title: Shine on Our Souls, Eternal God
description: Shine on Our Souls, Eternal God in Tonic Solfa to ST ANNE, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 42, “Doing All to God”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST ANNE; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Shine on our souls, E-ter-nal God, With rays of beau-ty shine; O, let Thy fa-vor crown our days, And all their round be Thine!

lines: Shine on our souls, Eternal God,
O, let Thy favor crown our days,
And all their round be Thine!
Did we not raise our hands to Thee,
Our hands might toil in vain;
Small joy success itself could give
With Thee let every week begin,
With Thee each day be spent,
For Thee each fleeting hour improved,
Since each by Thee is lent.
Midst hourly cares may love present
And while the world our hands employs,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST ANNE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
